fields.description:
## Context / Problem
The CI shell guard `[ -f <path> ] || { echo "… (change predates the gate) — skipping"; exit 0; }`
is written **24 times** across `.github/`: `_build-and-test.yml:145,159,181,195,210,288,377,570`;
`_optionality.yml:108,114,133`; `_mutation.yml:64`; `gerrit-verify.yaml:323,332`;
`.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` x10. It exists because a patchset whose base predates a
gate script must not fail `Verified` on that gate. Two defects came from copies drifting apart:
`anxious-resistant-urson` (a gate step with NO guard) and `sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly` (a guard
added late). The guard is also applied unevenly today — `test.yml:174,176` invoke
`scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` with no guard at all, while
`gerrit-verify.yaml:324,333` guard the same two scripts.

## Finding 1 — the CI guard CANNOT move into a shared repo file
A shared owner (composite action, shell helper, Python module) lives in the repo, so it is absent
on exactly the pre-gate trees the guard serves; the guard would then skip gates whose scripts DO
exist, or the job would fail resolving a missing local `uses:`. This is not a judgement call: the
existing pin `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_mutation_selector_skips_pre_gate_trees_without_weakening_current_trees`
executes the step's `run:` body under `bash` in an **empty directory** and requires exit 0 plus the
message on stdout — a body that shells out to a repo file cannot satisfy that. `gerrit-verify.yaml:206`
already carries the same exposure for `uses: ./.github/actions/docs-gates` itself.

## Finding 2 — the four gates ALREADY share one resolver
- Ref/source resolution is uniform: every gate, completion included, goes through
  `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:76`), completion reaching it at
  `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:149` via `close_autoresume.py:234`.
- Flag resolution for three of the four gates is one function, `gates.gate_enabled`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:91`), called from `gates.py:196` (plan-review close),
  `gates.py:282` (plan-review claim) and `close_precheck.py:489` (completion close).
- Its unreadable-config posture is already uniform and is **not** a warn-and-continue: it raises a
  chained `ConfigError` (`gates.py:115-120`), and `GateState` (`gates.py:49`) is two-state — the
  `UNREADABLE` member was REMOVED by operator ruling 39f8-ae7c. What differs between the three is
  only what each CALLER does with a `DISABLED` answer (`False` / a `"disabled"` payload /
  `"gate_off"`), which is caller policy, not a duplicated computation.
- The one separate reader, `code_review_enabled` (`llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:277`), must keep
  its divergence: its broad `except Exception` → silent `False` (`gate_dispatch.py:283-286`) is
  what degrades code review to inert; `gate_enabled` would instead raise, would warn, and would
  demand a `ticket_id` that code review — dispatching against a CHANGE — has no source for.

So the resolver named in this story's original plan would be pure indirection over an existing
shared implementation, with no behaviour change and no copy removed. It is dropped.

## Approach
Deliver the achievable equivalent of consolidation for a construct that cannot be shared: **one
owner for the invariant**, in the epic's guard shape — a test a drifting copy cannot pass.
Add `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`:

1. **Completeness.** For every `run:` step in the six files above that invokes a repo-relative
   `scripts/*.py` or reads a repo data file, assert the step body contains an `-f` test for that
   exact path together with the canonical `change predates the gate` message. A step that
   legitimately needs no guard carries `# predates-gate-ok: <reason>`; an empty or missing reason
   fails the test.
2. **Behaviour.** For every guarded step, execute its `run:` body (with `${{ … }}` expressions
   substituted to empty strings) under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` in an EMPTY
   directory with `GITHUB_OUTPUT` set, and assert exit 0 and the canonical message on stdout —
   generalising the single-site mutation pin above to all of them.

Guard form follows the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: match the conjunction
(`-f <path>` together with the canonical message), never one common token; mandatory-reason escape
marker; behaviour pinned only by the existing named tests.

## Constraint: four sites carry behaviour a bare skip would drop
`_mutation.yml:64` also writes `matrix={"shard":[]}` and `has-shards=false` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`;
`_optionality.yml:108,114` guard two generators **independently inside one step** per bug
`5bc6-5496-4e17-403a`; `_build-and-test.yml:181,195` use the inverted `[ -f ]/else` form with no
`exit 0`; `_build-and-test.yml:377` guards the DATA file `.github/git-version-floor.txt` and
continues into a `sort -V` that can `exit 1`. The test asserts the guard, never the step's shape,
so all four keep their current bodies.

## Constraint: no workflow behaviour changes in this story
This story adds no guard and removes none — adding a guard changes which gates run on an old
base, which is its own reviewable change. Every step the completeness check surfaces gets a
`# predates-gate-ok:` marker instead: for a step that needs no guard the reason says why, and for
a step that is a genuine gap the reason cites a ticket filed and linked `discovered_from` this
one. Workflow edits in this story are therefore comment-only.

## Scope
`tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` (new); `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`,
`_optionality.yml`, `_mutation.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `test.yml`,
`.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml` (comment-only `# predates-gate-ok:` markers, if needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every gate step in the six files either carries an `-f` guard naming the file it needs, or a
      `# predates-gate-ok:` marker with a non-empty reason; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py -k completeness`.
- [ ] Every guarded step body exits 0 and prints `change predates the gate` when run in an empty
      directory; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py -k empty_tree`.
- [ ] An escape marker whose reason is empty is rejected; checked by a negative case in that file
      feeding a synthetic step with a bare `# predates-gate-ok:` and asserting the check fails.
- [ ] A step that drops its guard is caught; checked by a negative case feeding a synthetic
      guard-free step and asserting the completeness check fails.
- [ ] No existing CI behaviour changes; checked by `git diff origin/main -- .github/` showing only
      comment lines, and by `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passing unchanged.
- [ ] Every marker whose reason cites a gap names a ticket linked `discovered_from` this one;
      checked by `rebar show 7e0d-7815-4425-4fdb` listing one link per such marker.
fields.title: Pin the predates-gate guard invariant across the Verified lane
